name: Replit Canvas Camera
move: editorial canvas thumbnails expand into a full product world, then the camera dives into a prompt and follows typing
how: A 2600×1500 HTML world sits beneath a deterministic camera. The opening holds a small pill-shaped canvas, then uses expoInOut focus moves to zoom into a modular brand board and pan between three web compositions. A warm-white flash clears the canvas into a restrained Replit Canvas wordmark. The second act cuts to a prompt UI; the camera moves from a wide centered view to a tight bottom-field crop while the sentence types and the send button lands with a spring. Every transform is derived from the render time—no CSS animation clock—so camera position, scale, focus blur and typing reproduce exactly under frame seeking.
adapt: Replace the modular cards with real product screenshots or DOM UI, and change the prompt string. Keep one dominant focus target per beat; preserve the 0.7–1.1s expo camera travel and the brief negative-space holds.
port: Mount the .world and .prompt-scene inside the shot. In animate(), drive one time proxy and call the same seek function. The camera target is a simple {x,y,zoom}; use Motion.camera on the scoped world element.
caveats: The brand-board artwork is programmatic HTML/CSS rather than copied footage
Uses a system/Atlas Grotesk approximation of Replit's native sans
